comments.text:
I’ve owned a construction company and part owner in a  oil field company and I sold my private equity stake in 2023. I’ve managed hundreds of roofers, carpenters, and welders. From actual experience, the idea that men enjoy brutal, back-breaking outdoor work is just wrong.

People do that kind of work because it pays well, not because they like it. It’s physically exhausting, hard on the body, dependent on weather, and comes with early mornings and real injury risk. If you told those same workers they could make the same money doing something indoors, climate-controlled, and easier on their bodies, almost all of them would take it immediately.

I’ve heard it directly from welders, roofers, and carpenters. Take away the hardship, and they’re gone. In my experience, easily 98% would switch to an inside job if the pay and stability were equal.

The people (Andrew)  who romanticize “working with your hands” or suffering through physical labor usually haven’t done it themselves. They talk about it in theory. The guys who’ve actually lived it don’t glorify it they do it until they can get out.
